To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) deep LSTM networks can be successfully trained for large vocabulary NMT tasks, (2) residual connections are important for training deep models, (3) the attention mechanism improves accuracy, (4) low precision arithmetic can be used during inference to speed up the translation, and (5) the word piece model can improve the accuracy of NMT

1) deep neural networks can be used to build practical and accurate machine translation systems that are on par or even better than phrase based systems; 2) low precision arithmetic can speed up inference by a factor of 3 with little loss in translation accuracy; 3) wordpiece models can improve the accuracy of neural machine translation systems; 4) beam search with coverage penalty can further improve translation quality.

1) a deep LSTM network using residual connections, 2) attention, 3) a bottom up top down attention connection, 4) low precision arithmetic, 5) wordpieces, and 6) length and coverage penalties can be combined to create an NMT system that can achieve competitive results to state-of-the-art, and that can be used in practical translation deployments and services.
